quotes.text: Copilot is becoming less like a search engine. You visit once and more like a collaborator. You keep coming back to.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Frames the shift from one-off AI answers to an ongoing collaborative work surface.

quotes.text: A page is a starting point, not a source of truth. Forget that and the page will happily carry a wrong number straight into your meeting.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A concise warning to verify AI-generated drafts before acting on them.

quotes.text: Copilot's answers depend on how rich and well-structured your underlying content is. Feed it thin, messy material and you get thin, generic pages. Feed it good files and the pages get sharper.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clearly links output quality to the quality of the underlying content.

quotes.text: Loop is for a living workspace a team keeps returning to. Notebooks are for a project you're still figuring out. Pages are for the artifact you actually hand to someone.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable rule of thumb for choosing between three similar Microsoft tools.

quotes.text: copilot pages isn't an Azure product, and that's not a flaw. It's a deliberate choice to put the AI where people already work, which is inside the tools they open every morning.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clarifies a common misconception and explains the product's design intent.

takeaways: Copilot Pages turns a temporary Copilot chat answer into a persistent, editable page you own and can refine side by side with Copilot.
Pages are shared like any Microsoft 365 file, support real-time co-authoring, inherit sensitivity labels and are stored in SharePoint Embedded, but cannot yet be opened by external guests.
Treat every page as a first draft: verify AI output, keep pages lean, and remember that results are only as good as the content you feed Copilot.
hook: Great Copilot answers vanish the moment you close the chat. This episode explains Copilot Pages for Microsoft 365 users who want to keep, refine and share AI output, how it differs from Loop and Copilot Notebooks, and the limits nobody mentions.
